summary:
Tocantins has no state statute of its own prohibiting discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity; the absence of such a law is recorded by the state's own Public Defender's Office. Protection in Palmas and across the interior therefore rests on Brazil's national framework, which applies here without any state-level variation. Same-sex marriage has applied in Tocantins since 2013 and joint adoption since 2010, under that national framework rather than any Tocantins enactment.

Name and gender-marker rectification in Tocantins is administrative. Trans men, trans women, non-binary, queer and travesti persons may request rectification of first name and/or gender marker at the civil registry where their birth was registered, on gender self-determination alone, with no medical or psychological report, no proof of surgery and no proof of hormonal treatment, following the Supreme Federal Court's understanding since 2018 and National Council of Justice norms. The change takes full legal effect in the birth certificate and in all official documents. The procedure is free on proof of inability to pay, and judicial recourse arises only if the request is denied. Rectification to a non-binary or unspecified gender is the exception: it requires a judicial decision.

Tocantins's own institutions have built the machinery for this. In August 2022 the Public Defender's Office of Tocantins asked the state General Inspectorate of Justice to authorise inclusion of the term "non-binary" in documents, and in 2023 the General Inspectorate published a resolution authorising non-binary people to change their documents to carry a third gender option. On 31 January 2023 the Corregedoria-Geral da Justiça of Tocantins issued Provimento No. 3, consolidating extrajudicial service norms and providing civil-registry procedures for registering a birth with a transgender parent and for the averbação of an altered first name and sex for transgender and non-binary persons. On 29 January 2026 the state Public Defender's Office published guidance explaining the name and gender-marker change process for trans people.

In Palmas, on 27 August 2018, Supreme Federal Court Justice Luís Roberto Barroso suspended the article of a municipal law that prohibited teaching about gender and sexuality in schools, allowing such teaching to proceed.
tangentialFactors:
A 2026 legal guide for foreign residents notes that enforcement of Brazil's protections is uneven in practice, contrasting major urban centres, with established legal infrastructure and broad acceptance, against smaller cities and rural areas where identical legal rights may still meet social friction. Within Tocantins that contrast bears directly on where a trans visitor can expect the registry procedures and documentation above to run smoothly: the institutional capacity sits in Palmas, while much of the state is small-town and rural.

Advances at national level face repeal pressure in a conservative Congress, and Brazil retains one of the world's highest rates of violence against sexual and gender minorities, particularly trans people, according to an international LGBTI rights organisation's country report of 12 March 2026. Those conditions shape the environment in which Tocantins's own protections operate, and the report separately records over 3,000 openly LGBTQ candidates in the 2024 municipal elections, a cycle that included Tocantins's municipalities.

Legal gender recognition by self-declaration has been the national standard since the Supreme Federal Court ruling of 1 March 2018, and trans voters in Tocantins may register under a lived name and identity even before their documents are updated.
localsOnly:
For residents, the practical route to a changed name and gender marker runs through the civil registry of the birth, administratively and without any clinical evidence, with the fee waived on proof of inability to pay. A refusal can be taken to a court; a change to non-binary or unspecified gender must go to a court from the outset, whatever the outcome for binary markers.

The state's 2023 General Inspectorate of Justice resolution authorising a third gender option on documents, and Provimento No. 3 of 31 January 2023 on extrajudicial registry services, are the instruments residents would invoke, the latter also covering registration of a birth where a parent is transgender. The Public Defender's Office of Tocantins is the state body publishing step-by-step guidance on the process, most recently on 29 January 2026.

Because Tocantins has enacted no anti-discrimination statute covering sexual orientation or gender identity, residents pursuing a discrimination complaint do so under the national framework rather than before a state authority.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory contains no Tocantins-specific assault, homicide or hate-crime figures, and no account of a discrimination case being brought or decided within the state; enforcement of the national framework in Tocantins is therefore unresolved on this sourcing.

How often the judicial route to a non-binary or unspecified marker has been used in Tocantins is not sourced, and nothing here documents whether the 2023 General Inspectorate of Justice resolution has been applied in practice or how registry officials in municipalities outside Palmas handle requests.

Whether Palmas's post-2018 school curricula in fact teach about gender and sexuality, and whether any other Tocantins municipality has comparable restrictive provisions, is not established by these sources.
